title: Expro secures its largest-ever Arctic project, supporting job growth in Alaska
summary: Multi-year North Slope contract will support workover and flowback operations.
body_markdown:
Expro (NYSE: XPRO), a leading provider of energy services, has secured a significant three-year contract with a major US operator to provide well flow management services across Alaska’s Arctic North Slope region.


It will be Expro’s largest-ever Arctic project, with the contract including two further one-year extension options.


Around 75 Expro field personnel are expected to support the contract once activity begins supporting the operator’s North Slope operations.


**Gregorio Rodrigues, Regional Vice President for North and Latin America at Expro, said:** “Securing our largest-ever Arctic project is a strong endorsement of the reputation our teams have built on the North Slope.


“Successful operations in Alaska demand specialized cold-weather equipment, detailed engineering and strong local knowledge. We look forward to bringing that capability to our client as the major oil drilling development moves forward, supporting safe, reliable and efficient operations.”


The contract covers Well Clean-up, Frac Flowback, Multi Phase Flow Meter and Solids Management across the operator’s North Slope operations.


From February 2028, Expro will also provide two flowback and well clean-up packages to support the development, where approximately 200 wells are planned. The scope will include a vapor recovery unit to help reduce the carbon footprint by capturing gas breakout in the tank farm, as well as wellhead, flare, nitrogen and fluid headers designed to improve efficiency and reduce non-operational time during moves between wells.


The development is expected to reach peak production of approximately 180,000 barrels of oil per day and has an expected field life of around 30 years. It is one of the largest oil developments on US public land in decades and is expected to become a major long-term source of domestic crude.


Expro has operated in Alaska since 2007, with an office in Anchorage and an operations base on the North Slope.


Over that period, Expro has supported approximately 85% of exploration and appraisal (E&A) wells drilled in Alaska.
